note: String skipping on the picking-drill (level advanced: down and up, two notes a string, a string skipped), then three notes a string so the jump leaves on a down stroke one time and an up stroke the next. The old tempo-ladder Stage selector is now moves (70 up to 90 for intermediate, up to 120 for advanced), so the text names the tempo only as {{=bpm}} and no selector. Folds in the three advanced versions as the advanced choice; one extra line per block.

exercise.title: Skip a string
exercise.why: Skipping a string makes the pick travel twice as far between notes, so it trains the aim that wide phrases across a position need.

cells.text:
Press Play below to start the metronome at {{=bpm}}. Pick down, up on one string, then jump over the next string to the one after it, as the tab shows. Keep the strokes small and let your wrist make the jump.
Practice until the pick lands on the right string without you looking at your picking hand.

Press Play below to start the metronome again. Now pick three notes on each string before the jump, and keep the strokes going down, up, down, up across it, as the arrows under the tab show: one jump leaves on a down stroke, the next on an up stroke.
If you hit the string in between, slow your hand down and aim for the far string before you pick.
